checks.why: an edit inside an arrow in a method body is a body change of THAT METHOD: every arrow carries one name, <arrow>, which is never the declaration an edit is charged to (its header was looked for by that name, not found, and the arrow came back removed)
the same for an unnamed function expression
an arrow on the one line of the function that holds it is that function's body
and what it reaches are that function's tests, not those of the same-shaped arrow in another file
an arrow no function encloses (handed over at the top level) is its own body change, named by where it is and targeted by file:line
control: an edit to a named function next to the arrows stays that function's
file:line on an arrow names that one arrow, by its enclosing method and line
and a function expression the same way
the name printed for an arrow is a target that answers for that arrow alone
